headline: Alphabet's record 12.6% plunge revives AI-spending fears; Nasdaq −1.4% as small caps rally
summary: A lopsided rotation day rather than a broad sell-off. Megacap tech and software slid from the open and the Nasdaq never recovered, but more than 400 S&P 500 members rose, the Russell 2000 gained 1% and Nasdaq advancers edged out decliners; healthcare led the sector table while communication services and tech fell the most, and the VIX rose only modestly to 17.20.
drivers: Google's parent fell 12.6%, erasing roughly $500 billion in value, after a slight revenue miss ($127.6 billion), a 114% jump in quarterly capex to $51.4 billion and negative free cash flow; it was the main drag on the indexes. Microsoft gave up an early earnings pop to close slightly lower, and a Bloomberg basket of AI winners fell 2.7%.

ServiceNow sank about 27% and Fortinet about 20% on soft guidance, revived fears of AI disruption in software and dragged Salesforce down 4.6%. The SOX fell 1.4%, ending a four-day run, as Micron dropped 5.0%, AMD 2.1% and Broadcom 1.9%, while Marvell slid about 13% on reports it is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum; Amazon lost 4.3% ahead of its results.
Hot growth, in-line PCE pull yields lower

Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace, the fastest in a year and above the 3.1% forecast, while September PCE prices rose 0.5% on the month for a 3.6% annual rate, roughly as expected. Treasuries still rallied on the tech-led haven bid: the 10-year fell about 5bp to 4.99% and the 2-year about 7bp to 4.67%.
Rotation into healthcare and small caps

Eli Lilly rose about 6% after raising its revenue outlook on weight-loss drug demand, helping healthcare lead, while Caterpillar dropped about 9.5% after holding its growth targets. Oil eased 0.8% to $102.00 as a renewed US push to restart Iran peace talks offset supply worries.
week: Four days into the week the S&P 500 is up 1.3%, the Nasdaq 0.9%, the Dow 0.2% and the Russell 2000 3.0%, leaving the S&P 500 about 1.2% below its Oct 5 record of 7,811.54; the backdrop is a 10-year yield near 5%, oil above $100 and a Fed leaning toward a December hike.
watch: Next: Friday's reaction to after-hours drops in Amazon (about −6% to −7% on heavy capex and a light Q4 outlook) and Intel (about −16% on a weak Q4 revenue guide), then the Nov 3 midterms and next week's October jobs report.
